title: How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay with Salary Packaging Companies in Australia
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes tax, super, and salary packaging companies in Australia.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year, assuming a standard full-time schedule.

faqs.q: What is salary packaging and how does it affect my hourly to annual calculation?
faqs.a: Salary packaging (also called salary sacrifice) lets you exchange part of your pre-tax salary for benefits like a car or electronic devices. It reduces your taxable income but does not change your super guarantee base, which is calculated on your ordinary earnings. When converting hourly to annual, your gross pay remains the same; packaging only affects your take-home pay after tax. For details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

faqs.q: How do I account for casual loading when converting hourly to annual?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. On the timesheet, check the 'casual loading' box to add 25% automatically. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading. For example, the National Minimum Wage base rate is $26.44; with loading it becomes $33.05. Your annual estimate will then reflect the loaded rate. See our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page for more.

faqs.q: What tax rates apply to my annual salary in 2026-27?
faqs.a: For 2026-27, the resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. This estimate does not include HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a detailed breakdown.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. The formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay would be twice the weekly amount: $26.44 × 38 × 2 = $2,009.44 per fortnight.

This conversion assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a baseline estimate. For a precise calculation, use [the timesheet](/), where you can enter your hourly rate and toggle casual loading.

### Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission and currently stands at $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week ($1,004.90 per week). However, many employees are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. Award rates vary by industry and occupation. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 (May 2026), but this is an average, not a median for any specific job.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. On the timesheet, a checkbox adds this loading automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.** For example, the casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When converting to annual, use the loaded rate if you are casual.

### Superannuation and Salary Packaging

Superannuation Guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your hourly rate; it is an additional cost to the employer. For an employee earning the National Minimum Wage, the employer would contribute $6,269.45 per year (12% of $52,245.44).

If you are considering **salary packaging companies in australia**, remember that salary packaging reduces your taxable income but does not change your super guarantee base. Your ordinary earnings for super purposes remain the same. Salary packaging can be a tax-effective way to pay for items like cars, laptops, or childcare, but it does not affect the hourly-to-annual conversion itself. For more, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax Considerations

Your annual gross salary is used to calculate income tax. For the 2026-27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The tax-free threshold is included. This estimate does not account for HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a detailed take-home estimate, visit the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Using the Timesheet

The [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and select whether you are casual (adding 25% loading). It then calculates your annual gross, fortnightly pay, superannuation (12% on top), and estimated tax. The results are based on the assumptions above and the 2026-27 tax rates. Remember that this is an estimate only. For award-specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

Always consult the Fair Work Ombudsman for your correct minimum entitlement and the Australian Taxation Office for your personal tax situation.
